scope: Proposition 7.8 (Uniform perturbation) of the manuscript “Weak pure infiniteness and O-infinity absorption” (preprints/Weak-pure-infiniteness-and-O-infinity-absorption-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 303 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2de287a58acb7170), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 36. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let C be an exact C∗-algebra satisfying (Fn) for one fixed integer n ≥ 1. Let p, q ∈ C be contractions and let h, k, c ∈ C+ satisfy p∗ ph = h, qq∗ k = k, c⊕n ≾ h, c⊕n ≾ k. (7.13) For every T ∈ C and every η, α > 0, there is a contraction y ∈ C such that ∥(T + ηpyq)P ∥ ≥ ση for every P ∈ Prim(C) with ∥cP ∥ ≥ α. (7.14) If h, k belong to a hereditary subalgebra D ⊂ C, then y may be chosen in D. If, in addition or independently, p, q are positive and pq = 0, then y may be chosen selfadjoint. Both conclusions may be imposed simultaneously. The constant σ is independent of all the data in the Proposition, including n and the norms of T, h, k, c.
